chunks: What Saʿd narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from ʿAlī ibn Sālim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: Do I perform tayammum and pray, then later find water while there is still time remaining for me? He said: “Do not repeat the salat, for indeed the Lord of water is the Lord of the earth.”

Then Dāwūd ibn Kathīr al-Raqqī said to him: Should I seek water to the right and the left? He said: “Do not seek water to the right or the left, nor in a well. If you find it on the road, then perform wudu (ablution); and if you do not find it, then proceed.”
Because the basis for understanding this report is the state of fear and necessity, and that which indicates that tayammum is only obligatory at the end of the time.

key_terms.آخِرِ الْوَقْتِ: the end of the prayer time, when tayammum becomes due according to the cited indication
key_terms.أَتَيَمَّمُ: I perform tayammum, the dry ablution used when water is unavailable
key_terms.الصَّعِيدِ: the earth or clean ground used for tayammum
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the obligatory salat performed after purification
key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: necessity that qualifies the circumstances of the report
key_terms.الْخَوْفِ: a state of fear affecting the legal application of the ruling
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water used for purification such as wudu (ablution)
key_terms.فَتَوَضَّأْ: then perform wudu (ablution) if water is found

ai.seo_question: If someone prays with tayammum and then finds water before the prayer time ends, must the salat be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of tayammum when water is unavailable and clarifies that a prayer performed with tayammum does not need to be repeated if water is found afterward within the prayer time. It also indicates that one is not required to search extensively for water in every direction, while the closing note explains that this report is understood in a circumstance of fear and necessity and points to tayammum being due at the end of the time.
